name: NJ-08
label: Safe D

key_factors: Incumbent Rob Menendez running with large financial advantage
No Republican on ballot; independent challengers with no fundraising
Prediction markets price Democratic win at ~95%
model.rationale: The baseline model's D+23 margin rests on a D+15 partisan lean, incumbency, and a dominant fundraising edge, with no credible opposition on the ballot. Polymarket's 95% Democratic win probability corroborates a Safe D rating, so I keep the baseline essentially unchanged.
model.watch: Any late-breaking scandal or a well-funded independent surge could narrow the margin, though a Democratic loss remains highly unlikely.
notes: No expert rater lists this race; treated as safe for the party holding the seat.
No usable general-election polls; forecast rests on fundamentals and expert ratings.
Aristotle Eliopoulos is an independent standing in for the Republican side.

overview:
NJ-08 is a heavily Democratic Hudson County-area seat with a D+15 partisan lean. Incumbent Rob Menendez is running for renomination and reelection with roughly $2 million raised and outside support, while his general-election opposition consists of independents with no reported fundraising or outside spending, and no Republican appears on the ballot.

With no public polling and no expert ratings, the forecast leans on fundamentals: the district lean, incumbency, and the incumbent's financial edge point to a margin in the low-to-mid 20s. Prediction markets put the Democratic win probability around 95%, consistent with a Safe D rating. The main uncertainty is the absence of polling, which keeps the confidence at medium despite the lopsided fundamentals.
